observations.text: Re-review scope and byte state. argv "git rev-parse HEAD" prints c03bed6a1465bbf72aa09c579318c3abe47ea59a and argv "git status --porcelain" exits 0 with empty output, so the oracle and its supports are judged by their committed bytes. Mechanical selection of the test files changed since the revision of the accepted r1 review: argv "git diff --name-only 9de297d HEAD", exit 0, names exactly three files under crates/: src/steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs, src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs and tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature, all three declared oracle or supports of this slice; the fourth declared support, crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/external_integration_plugins.rs, is unchanged, so the reviewed set is complete. The feature-file delta is exactly two items: the S1 remediation of the r1 finding (one step added at line 1119) and one new S2 scenario at line 1346. argv "git diff 9de297d HEAD -- docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/acceptance.md | grep ^@@" prints hunks only at lines 240 and above, while S1 occupies acceptance.md lines 5-229, so no S1 acceptance row changed; the brief.md and architecture.md deltas touch only I-31, the live-replica sentence and the start-over state (P6, D6), none of the S1 promises P1-P5, P10 and P11. Scope is therefore the S1 remediation plus every other delta of this commit that reaches an S1 row; every other judgment of the r1 and b5d86c6 reviews is retained unchanged, including criteria adequacy against the agreed value, the driving-port boundary and closure for E1-E6, E8-E10, E23, E24 and the justified NotTested at the public port for P3.

Own run of the selected oracle at this revision. argv: timeout 2400 scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c "export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4; source scripts/eip-lanes.sh; eip_warm; eip_lane us-iis-07", log /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-canzan-foundry/37002247-a143-4768-8211-686d885a6706/scratchpad/s1-r2-lane.txt, exit 101. The tag selection is the whole US-IIS-07 set, so S1 and S2 run together. stdout summary: "1 feature / 21 scenarios (12 passed, 9 failed) / 303 steps (294 passed, 9 failed)" and "9 step(s) failed, 0 parsing error(s), 0 hook error(s)"; no stderr beyond the cargo test failure line, warm build inside the VM and the warm attempt at 0s. All 11 S1 scenario executions passed: the walking scenario, the four counts of the replace-page outline, the three counts of the confirm outline, the reload scenario, the two-replica race and the CLI rotation. All 9 failures belong to S2, each the start-over door answering 404 Not Found at /admin/instance/integrations/secrets-key/start-over or the Start over offer being absent: missing production behaviour of S2, not infrastructure, and no S1 row among them. 0 parsing and 0 hook errors establish mechanically that the new step texts of this commit, including "Priya is offered a way to replace the secrets key" beside the shipped quoted-button step and "posts a start over request anyway", introduced no undefined or ambiguous step for any S1 step text. S1 own semantic RED stays the measured one of the accepted b5d86c6 review (~/.cache/nwdes/iis-secrets-key-replace/s1-red-2.txt, EXIT=101, 11 of 11 scenarios failing on the replace door answering 404 through the production router); S1 production behaviour shipped at d34ab3a, so GREEN here is that RED completion observation, not a new RED claim.

The remediation closes the open finding of the r1 review, and its falsifier direction is observed in this same run rather than argued. The r1 finding was that making the shared open-replace step follow a redirection left the four counts of the replace-page outline with no assertion on the answer path, so a door answering the replace address with a redirect to /admin/instance/integrations and rendering the I-23 sentence there would pass every count. The commit adds exactly the prescribed step: feature line 1119 now reads "Then Priya is on the replace secrets key page" above "And Priya reads \"<sentence>\"", bound at steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs:665 to then_on_replace_page (support/instance_integration_setup.rs:2779), which asserts answer.status.is_success() && answer.path.split('?').next() == Some(REPLACE_DOOR). argv "grep -n 'is on the replace secrets key page' crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature" prints lines 1084 and 1119, both S1, and the lane log shows the step passing five times (log lines 72, 109, 130, 151, 172): once in the walking scenario for n = 3 and once in each of the four counts n = 0, 1, 1, 2. That the wrong behaviour now fails is observed, not deduced: eip::follow (support/external_integration_plugins.rs:846) re-GETs the Location, so the followed answer carries the redirect target as its path, and the S2 scenario at feature line 1325 drives the very same when_open_replace in a state where the shipped door does redirect - it is the one S2 scenario that passed in this run (log line 493), its answer being this Foundry integrations page. In that state then_on_replace_page predicate is false, so the n = 0, n = 1 and n = 2 forms of E2 have their falsifier back, for an answer shape this oracle actually produces elsewhere in the same run.

The other delta that reaches S1 rows strengthens them: the reading doors now compare the config version. remember() (support/instance_integration_setup.rs:2678) gains world.iis.version_before from stored_config_version, which reads store.config_version() (crates/foundry-store/src/integrations/instance.rs:409, present at this commit), and then_nothing_replaced now also asserts version_now == version_before with a WHAT/WHY/HOW message naming the prefetch and the rebuild every server would do for a change nobody made. Both S1 uses of that step - feature line 1089 in the walking scenario and line 1124 in the outline - are reached with version_before set, because the preceding When of each is when_choose_key_control (line 1081) or when_open_replace (line 1118), both of which call remember() before the GET of the replace door, while the intervening "opens the instance integrations page" When is when_open, which does not remember; the five passing executions in this run confirm the .expect() is never hit. This closes a clause of the S1 design falsifier that previously had no observation: "A prefetch of the confirm page that bumps the config version or replaces the key", and the S1 design Expected "leaves the stored key id, the activity list and the config version unchanged after both GETs". The two-GET form is honest for the same reason the r1 review gave for the one-shot notice: when_choose_key_control re-remembers between the prefetch GET and the control GET, so the comparison spans the second GET only, but both GETs are identical requests to the same door and handler, and the outline exercises that door as the first read of its scenario for all four counts, so a bump on either read is observed somewhere in the row set.

Every remaining delta of this commit judged against the S1 rows, and none of them reaches one. (1) The new S2 scenario at feature line 1346 and the steps it needs - InstanceDoor::StartOver with START_OVER_DOOR and no posted fields, Button::way, Offer::of_way, the "start over" arm of the post-door regex - are additive arms of closed types; no shipped arm changed its path, label or fields, and argv greps place "posts a start over request anyway" at feature line 1357 only. (2) then_way_to_start_over became then_way_to over a Button, with a generalised message that still states WHAT, WHY and HOW; argv "grep -n 'is offered a way|is offered no way'" places its scenario uses at feature lines 1215, 1244, 1263, 1284, 1352 and 1353, all S2, and the shipped "<who> is offered no way to enter the Slack app" step keeps its own disjoint regex. S1 reads the offer through the quoted-button step at steps line 291, untouched. (3) TICKS was replaced by await_beats, a bounded poll on integration_replica_states, used by given_other_server_opens_key and given_a_minute_passes; argv "grep -n 'a minute passes'" places every use at feature lines 1212 and above, so no S1 scenario waits on a beat, and judging that construction belongs to the S2 review running concurrently on the same commit. (4) IisState gains version_before and other_server_running; its manual Debug is formatted in no assertion message of the acceptance crate, so no S1 failure message lost content. (5) when_post_door now remembers for StartOver as well as Replace: argv greps place the replace-request and start-over-request step texts at feature lines 1334 and 1357, both S2.

One record asymmetry, noted rather than raised as a defect. The commit updated six S2 acceptance rows to read "the stored key, the Activity and the version every replica follows are as they were", while the two S1 rows that drive the same strengthened step still read "the stored key and the whole Activity list are as they were before both readings" (acceptance.md S1 row 1) and "the stored key and the whole Activity list are unchanged afterwards" (S1 row 2). Closure still holds in both directions: the version observation maps to the S1 design Expected and falsifier, which both name the config version, so no obligation lacks a falsifier and no observation lacks an obligation. What is understated is only the row prose a later completion reader consults. The remedy, if the owner wants the record symmetric, is to name the version in those two S1 Expected texts when the acceptance record is next revised; this review does not treat it as a finding.

typesafe: unavailable at this revision. argv "python /Users/jeffbailey/.claude/skills/nw-typesafe-system-one/scripts/jev_decide.py --request - --output -" with the request on stdin from a shell heredoc - a batch of two reviewer-owned Noul questions: whether the outline assertion set with the added address pin fails for a door that redirects to the integrations page carrying the I-23 sentence, and whether the re-read of key, activity and config version observes every clause of the no-change promise for the single GET it performs - exits 3 with "TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment". argv "zsh -lc 'test -n "$TYPESAFE_API_KEY" ...'" prints KEY_ABSENT, so the key is absent from the login environment too, not only from a tool kernel. No call was fabricated and no producer-owned judgment was reused; both questions were resolved locally from the oracle bytes and from this run own evidence (R3, R4). Code facts came from the project port: argv "code-fact query.callers-of then_on_replace_page --root crates/foundry-acceptance" answered provider textsearch, confidence noisy, index live-source, coverage empty, sites steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs:667 and support/instance_integration_setup.rs:2779 - a degraded lexical answer that may over-report strings and comments and miss indirect uses, cross-checked against the feature file with argv "grep -n 'is on the replace secrets key page'", which prints lines 1084 and 1119. No timing claim is made: no S1 test is at half budget and no derogation is in force, so no nine-run measurement was taken.

Current comparison justifying reuse of the run of R2, after the oracle file changed under this review. While the observations above were being recorded the working tree went dirty: argv "git status --porcelain" now prints " M crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature", " M docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/runs/review.oracle.S2.json" and the untracked draft directory, HEAD still c03bed6a1465bbf72aa09c579318c3abe47ea59a. The S2 oracle owner is correcting the S2 findings in the file this slice shares with S2, concurrently with this review. The uncommitted delta does not reach S1: argv "git diff -U0 -- crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature | grep ^@@" prints hunks at 1283, 1343 and 1357 only - one added I-26-absence assertion in the S2 I-31 scenario and the removal of the start-over post from the new S2 scenario - while every S1 scenario lies between lines 1070 and 1200. The S1 bytes are identical to the ones run: argv "git show HEAD:...feature | sed -n 1,1200p | shasum -a 256" and argv "sed -n 1,1200p ...feature | shasum -a 256" both print 54520e063d22cc9d9eb6c3523f9df6a5eed286ffb3100424ce6e0310d3e17efc, and argv "git status --porcelain -- crates/foundry-acceptance/src/" prints nothing, so both changed supports are unmodified since the run. No check is restamped as a new execution: the run cited in R2 is the one at the committed bytes of c03bed6, exit 101, and the relevant inputs of every S1 judgment - the S1 region of the oracle, both supports, the production source and the runtime - are unchanged against it, so no affected check has to run again. The S2 rows this delta does change are not this review's subject; the concurrent S2 reviewer judges them.

diagnostic:
Accepted at c03bed6, no findings open. The one finding of the r1 review is closed by the remediation it asked for, and the rest of this commit either leaves the S1 rows alone or strengthens them.

Scope was mechanically bounded. Three test files changed since 9de297d, all three declared oracle or supports of this slice, and the fourth declared support is unchanged. The feature-file delta is exactly the S1 remediation at line 1119 and one new S2 scenario at line 1346. No S1 acceptance row changed - every acceptance.md hunk sits at line 240 or above while S1 occupies lines 5-229 - and the brief and architecture deltas touch only I-31, the live-replica sentence and the start-over state, none of the S1 promises. Every other judgment of the earlier reviews is retained: criteria adequacy against the agreed value (rotate the key the moment she doubts it, without making any workspace reconnect), the driving-port boundary, and closure for E1-E6, E8-E10, E23, E24 and the justified NotTested at the public port for P3.

The remediation is the prescribed step, and its falsifier direction is observed in this run rather than argued. Feature line 1119 now pins the address through then_on_replace_page, which asserts success and a path equal to the replace door, and the step passes five times in the log: the walking scenario for n = 3 and each of the four counts. The wrong behaviour the r1 finding named is produced by this oracle elsewhere in the same run - the S2 scenario at line 1325 drives the same when_open_replace in a state where the shipped door does redirect, and eip::follow re-GETs the Location, so its answer path is the integrations page, which the predicate rejects. The n = 0, n = 1 and n = 2 forms of E2 have their falsifier back.

The second delta reaching S1 strengthens it. remember() now also records the config version and then_nothing_replaced asserts it unchanged, with a WHAT/WHY/HOW message. Both S1 uses are reached with the version remembered before the replace-door GET, which closes a clause of the S1 design falsifier that had no observation until now: a prefetch of the confirm page that bumps the config version.

Everything else of this commit is S2 work: additive arms of InstanceDoor, Button and Offer, the generalised offer step used only at feature lines 1215 and above, the bounded beat poll that replaced the fixed wait, two new IisState fields formatted in no assertion message, and the remembered start-over post. Each was checked against the S1 line ranges by argv grep, and none appears in an S1 scenario.

Evidence: own run at this revision, argv timeout 2400 scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c "export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4; source scripts/eip-lanes.sh; eip_warm; eip_lane us-iis-07", exit 101, "21 scenarios (12 passed, 9 failed) / 303 steps (294 passed, 9 failed) / 0 parsing error(s), 0 hook error(s)". All 11 S1 scenario executions passed; all 9 failures are S2 missing start-over behaviour, which also establishes that the new step texts left no S1 step undefined or ambiguous. S1's own semantic RED remains the measured one at b5d86c6 (11 of 11 failing on the replace door answering 404 through the production router); production shipped at d34ab3a, so GREEN here is that RED's completion observation.

Two limits are on the record rather than hidden. The oracle file went dirty under this review, the S2 owner correcting S2 findings in the file S1 shares with S2; R8 records the comparison that lets the run stand - the S1 region of the file, lines 1 to 1200, hashes identically to the committed bytes that were run, both supports are unmodified, and the three uncommitted hunks are at lines 1283 and above. And typesafe: unavailable (exit 3, key absent in the login environment), so both reviewer questions were answered locally from the oracle bytes and this run; code facts came from code-fact at noisy confidence over live source, cross-checked against the feature file. One record asymmetry is noted as an observation, not a finding: the two S1 acceptance rows still describe only the key and the Activity while their step now also compares the version, which the six updated S2 rows do name.
